podcast.body: Released in 1996, this album followed the band's near-breakup and contractual struggles with Geffen, almost becoming a Geffen release before they moved to The Enclave, a short-lived boutique label, and was released on Murder Records in Canada. Uniquely, the album was recorded with members in different locations, as Chris, Jay, and Patrick laid down instrumental parts in Toronto, then sent tapes to Andrew in Halifax for drum tracks. It earned a respectable three and a half out of five stars from Rolling Stone Magazine, won a Juno Award, and helped solidify their fanbase in the US, despite its American label collapsing. "Sloan from their 1996 album One Cord to Another, everything you've done wrong."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
